item.headline: Ohio to pause tax incentives for future data centers
causal_chain: Ohio pauses tax incentives for new data center development, raising effective cost of capital for projects in the state
Hyperscalers and colocation operators face higher all-in costs on Ohio-sited expansion; project timelines extend or relocate, compressing near-term revenue pipeline for power and land adjacent plays

CEG derives meaningful utility-scale power purchase agreement (PPA) pipeline from data center co-location demand in PJM territory (which includes Ohio); a slowdown in Ohio data center permitting reduces incremental PPA demand and re-rates near-term contract flow
item.directional_bias: bearish data center infrastructure build-out; modest headwind to PJM nuclear power demand narrative

sizing_recommendation.rationale: Single-state regulatory action with ambiguous scope; causal chain to CEG earnings is real but attenuated — Ohio is one node in a national PPA pipeline. Signal is too thin for a reduce on a held position; monitor for broadening to other states before acting.

item.reasoning: Ohio's pause on data center tax incentives is a Layer 0/2 signal — a regulatory action that marginally raises the cost of data center buildout in a key PJM geography. CEG is the most directly connected portfolio holding because its power-demand thesis is built substantially on hyperscaler PPA growth in the Mid-Atlantic/Midwest corridor. However, this is a single-state action of uncertain duration and scope, and the causal chain from state tax policy pause to CEG revenue impact requires multiple conditional steps (projects actually cancel vs. relocate, PPA volume actually declines, CEG specifically loses contracts vs. competitors). Confidence is capped at 0.38 given low_specificity and forward_looking_only flags. No reduce warranted at this signal strength; the thesis is not invalidated, but the item belongs on the watchlist for escalation.

item.headline: Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness fund discloses 5.6% stake in Nebius Group
causal_chain: High-profile AI investor (former OpenAI safety lead, author of 'Situational Awareness' memo) discloses meaningful stake in Nebius Group — a European GPU cloud and AI infrastructure operator
Institutional signal from a credible AI-specialist investor increases visibility on Nebius as a non-US AI infrastructure proxy, drawing coverage and potential follow-on flows

Nebius operates on NVIDIA hardware; increased investor interest in the name is a marginal positive read-through for AI infrastructure demand broadly, though effect on NVDA is second-order and negligible
item.directional_bias: bullish NBIS specifically; thematic confirmation of AI infrastructure demand cycle

sizing_recommendation.rationale: No portfolio exposure to NBIS; signal is a single institutional disclosure with no multi-layer confluence. Thematic read-through to held names (MSFT, CEG) is too attenuated to act on.

item.reasoning: Aschenbrenner's fund disclosure is a Layer 2 insider/institutional signal on a radar name (Nebius) not in the portfolio. The credibility of the investor adds some weight — this is not a random 13F — but the stake is a disclosed position rather than a fresh catalyst, and Nebius itself is a small-cap European cloud operator with limited liquidity. No portfolio holdings are directly affected. The thematic link to AI infrastructure demand is real but too diffuse to move the needle on MSFT or CEG sizing. Filed as watch-list context only.
